content: are there screws supposed to be tighten? They need to be somewhat loose for the alightment, but the once the alignment is done you do not have access to them.  Thus, should the bed be alittle loose in the end

This is more a comment on the combined INDX/Gen2 upgrade as a whole rather than this guide/step in particular, but we shouldn't be 'placing' the spacer there and then just leaving it completely unsecured for multiple steps while bouncing between the other guides, that's just asking for a tiny one-of part to get bumped/lost.

Why face the joints out? All this does is ensure when you push the aligner in on the next steps, the joints pop off the bed and you have to disassemble the whole thing again to replace them.

Sometimes I don't think Prusa test their guides. fml

I used the M3x14bT from the next step and screwed it in about half way from underneath, placed the spacer over the top, then placed the heatbed on top aligning the hole and without moving the bed unscrew the bolt from underneath and screw it in from the top.

I've found attaching the bed easier if the center spacer can't move. What's worked for me is to apply two or three tiny drops of CA glue on the face of one end of the spacer. Thread the heatbed mounting screw through the spacer and tighten against the heatbed frame with the glue between the spacer and the frame. (The countersink shape on the underside of the headbed mounting screw should help center the spacer.) Let the CA glue cure for about a minute or more while you do other things. Remove the headbed mounting screw and continue with assembly.

Please be careful not to use too much CA glue as you don't want any squeeze out to glue the heatbed mounting screw in place...

I've been using this technique since the MK3 days and it has proven useful for me.
